name: Food Safety Officer
title: Food Safety Officer (FSS Act)
intro: From Class 12 Science to a Food Safety Officer: a degree listed in the FSS Rules, 2011, your state's FSO recruitment, appointment and training by the Commissioner of Food Safety, then Designated Officer.

phases.title: Class 12 Science
phases.summary: PCB or PCM leads to the eligible degrees.
points: Class 12 Science (PCB or PCM) leads to food technology, microbiology, biotechnology, agriculture and similar degrees.
Commerce and Arts do not lead to the listed degrees.
Choose the degree with the FSS Rules list in mind.

phases.title: An eligible degree
phases.summary: A degree listed in the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.
points: Listed degrees include food technology, dairy technology, biotechnology, oil technology, agricultural science, veterinary science, biochemistry, microbiology, a master's in chemistry, or medicine.
A B.Sc Chemistry alone may not be enough — the Rules mention a master's in chemistry; check your state notice.
Private food companies hire quality and regulatory staff with the same degrees.

phases.title: State FSO recruitment
phases.summary: A written exam, and an interview where applicable.
points: States recruit FSOs through their PSCs or recruitment boards; read each notice.
Age, domicile and other conditions are set in each state's notice.
FSSAI recruits its own technical and central posts separately.

phases.title: Appointment and training
phases.summary: Appointed by the state Commissioner of Food Safety; trained as the Food Authority specifies.
points: The FSS Act, 2006 creates FSSAI and the food safety officer system in every state.
Training after appointment is specified by the Food Authority.
FSO pay follows each state's pay rules; FSSAI posts follow the central pay matrix.

phases.title: Grow
phases.summary: Designated Officer and senior food safety roles.
points: Growth path: FSO → Designated Officer → senior food safety administration.
Employers beyond government: food manufacturers, QA labs, regulatory consultancies, hotels and restaurant chains.
FSSAI sets the food standards you enforce — keep up with its updates.
